source_basis: Paper filters successful passes and builds a directed weighted graph per match with node position from average pass coordinates.
interpretation: A match-level passing network can serve as the sole data object for team performance analysis when all subsequent metrics are readings of that one graph.
applicability: Any sport or cooperative task with pairwise event logs.
counterevidence: The network ignores unsuccessful passes, off-ball movement and defensive actions, so it captures only one channel of cooperation.

source_basis: Centroid is the weighted mean position of all passes; dispersion is the weighted standard deviation of player distances from the centroid.
interpretation: A single spatial summary (centroid + dispersion) compresses a match network into a position spread indicator that can be compared across matches.
applicability: Any spatial network where node positions are meaningful.
counterevidence: Centroid is sensitive to outlier long passes and ignores the time dimension.

source_basis: Ucinet software partitions players into 10 core and 4 periphery members based on the weighted adjacency matrix.
interpretation: The binary partition gives a structural role assignment that feeds the midfielders/core ratio indicator.
applicability: Any network with a hub-and-spoke hypothesis.
counterevidence: Body says 10 core players; appendix R code hard-codes 12. The discrepancy is never resolved.

source_basis: The paper uses the thirteen canonical three-node directed subgraph types as a vocabulary for local network structure.
interpretation: Motif frequencies characterise local passing patterns; motif 12 and 13 (highest connectivity) are selected for the configuration ratio.
applicability: Any directed network where triadic closure matters.
counterevidence: The appendix R code counts four-node subgraphs (size=4), not three-node, and keeps only the maximum, so it cannot reproduce the reported statistics.

source_basis: Fig6 shows motif 12 dominates across 38 matches; the connected configuration ratio is defined as (freq_motif12 + freq_motif13) / total_freq.
interpretation: Selecting the two most-connected three-node types as a ratio gives a single scalar for team passing flexibility.
applicability: D problems using motif census in any network domain.
counterevidence: Selection of exactly two motifs out of thirteen is not justified by a statistical test; the choice is motivated by connectivity rank alone.

source_basis: Three individual indicators (pi1=total passes, pi2=CV of passes, pi3=midfielders/core) and four team-level processes (tp1=dispersion, tp2=max radius, tp3=time to 50th pass, tp4=configuration ratio).
interpretation: Seven indicators cover three scales (individual, spatial, temporal) of team performance, each derived from a network reading.
counterevidence: The seven indicators are not orthogonal; several share the adjacency matrix as input, creating potential collinearity.

source_basis: Figure 8 scatter plots show pi2 and tp1 have no visible trend against goal difference; both are removed before regression.
interpretation: Visual screening is a legitimate pre-regression step but the removal decision is subjective with no formal test reported.
counterevidence: No correlation coefficient or significance test accompanies the visual removal.

interpretation: The first fit keeps five predictors; only tp3 and tp4 are significant at 0.05. Pi1's negative coefficient contradicts the expected positive association with total passes.
counterevidence: The paper discards pi1 for its sign, not its p-value; tp2 with p=0.111 is kept in the second fit despite being insignificant in the first.

source_basis: reg score tp2 tp3 tp4, r: n=38, F(3,34)=13.05, R2=0.4138, RMSE=1.536. All three significant: tp2 p=0.013, tp3 p=0.001, tp4 p=0.004.
interpretation: The reduced model trades R2 (0.4656 to 0.4138) for parsimony and significance of all retained predictors.
counterevidence: The prose describes R2=0.4138 as 'a high level' without noting the drop from 0.4656; RMSE also worsened.

source_basis: Figure 10 shows VIF values for tp2, tp3, tp4 all below the conventional threshold, confirming no multicollinearity.
interpretation: Low VIF supports the claim that the three indicators measure distinct aspects of team performance.
counterevidence: VIF checks only pairwise collinearity, not predictive validity or out-of-sample performance.

source_basis: Page 12 says 'the F-value was significantly lower than 0.05'. The F statistic is 13.05; Prob>F=0.0000 is what is below 0.05.
interpretation: Confusing a test statistic with its p-value is a fundamental reporting error that undermines the statistical argument.
counterevidence: None; the error is unambiguous.

source_basis: The second regression has R2=0.4138 (down from 0.4656) but is described as 'showing a high level' without comparison to the first fit.
interpretation: Reporting only the surviving model's R2 without the first fit's higher value hides the cost of variable removal.
counterevidence: None; the first R2 is printed in Figure 9 on the same page.

source_basis: Pi1 correlation 0.32 placed in band 0.3<0.32<0.8 to argue weak positive; pi3 correlation 0.05 is discarded. The band boundaries are arbitrary.
interpretation: Variable retention after regression exclusion uses an unstated threshold rather than a formal test.
counterevidence: No cited source for the 0.3 and 0.8 thresholds.

source_basis: The paper ranks the Huskies on three aspects: extension 2nd/20, configuration ratio 15th/20, tempo (time to 50 passes) 7th/20.
interpretation: Converting regression coefficients into aspect rankings gives actionable feedback: strong spatial spread, weak triadic passing, moderate tempo.
applicability: D problems converting model outputs into ranked performance profiles.
counterevidence: Rankings are computed from 38 matches of a single season with no confidence intervals.

source_basis: Three recommendations: strengthen three-member group cooperation (motif 12+13), improve passing consistency, and avoid fast opening tempo against strong opponents.
interpretation: Each recommendation traces to a regression coefficient and a rank, making the advice auditable.
counterevidence: The tempo recommendation relies on a negative coefficient whose causal mechanism is assumed, not tested.

source_basis: Four indicators mapped to general teamwork properties: interaction frequency, task coverage, gradual pacing, subgroup communication. Three unmeasured factors added.
interpretation: Abstracting sport-specific indicators into domain-general properties is a legitimate extension, but the mapping is asserted, not validated.
counterevidence: No external data or domain-expert validation supports the generalized reading.

source_basis: The strategy paragraph at bottom of page 12 is repeated almost verbatim at top of page 13 with minor rewording.
interpretation: A copy-paste artefact across a page break that was never cleaned up.
applicability: Writing quality control in any paper.
counterevidence: None; the duplication is visible in the PDF.

source_basis: Body identifies 10 core players; appendix R code hard-codes 12 including two the body classifies as periphery.
interpretation: The indicator pi3 (midfielders/core) uses a denominator that differs between body and appendix, making all 38 values potentially wrong.
counterevidence: None; the two lists are printed and incompatible.

source_basis: R code calls graph.motifs(network,size=4) counting four-node subgraphs, but the paper's vocabulary is thirteen three-node types.
interpretation: The appendix code cannot reproduce the motif statistics the paper reports; tp4 is not reproducible.
counterevidence: None; the function signature is unambiguous.

source_basis: Fig7 caption repeats Fig6 caption verbatim; Fig7 content is a timeline, not a motif chart.
interpretation: Caption duplication is a proofreading failure that misleads caption-scanning readers.
counterevidence: None.

source_basis: Page 7 says 'shown in figure 4' for the motif catalogue, but it is printed as Fig5. Fig4 is the core-periphery table.
interpretation: Wrong cross-reference points reader to the wrong figure.
counterevidence: None.

source_basis: Section 4.5.2 contains multiple syntactically broken sentences that appear to be rough machine translation.
interpretation: The technical argument about triadic configurations is unparseable; meaning must be inferred from surrounding context.
applicability: Writing quality in non-native English papers.
counterevidence: None.

source_basis: All seven indicators and all six models derive from a single match-level passing network, creating a clean dependency chain.
interpretation: Using one data object as the root of all metrics simplifies traceability but concentrates fragility: any network construction error propagates to every downstream result.
applicability: D problems using a single-source dependency chain.
counterevidence: The network omits unsuccessful passes, off-ball events and defensive data.

source_basis: tp3 = time to first 50 passes in a match; shorter time means faster opening tempo. Coefficient is negative in both regressions.
interpretation: A negative coefficient for tempo means faster opening hurts goal difference, a counterintuitive finding the paper correctly preserves rather than discarding.
applicability: Any temporal indicator in sports analytics.
counterevidence: The 50-pass threshold is arbitrary; the paper does not test sensitivity to this choice.

source_basis: Abstract opens with a stakes claim needing no data, then routes each task by its own heading word, ending with direct advice to the addressee.
interpretation: The stakes-first abstract pattern compresses the full argument into six blocks that give the reader the indicator-to-recommendation mapping before any section.
applicability: D abstracts that must compress a network analysis into a recommendation.
counterevidence: The compression loses all uncertainty language.

source_basis: Each network object is introduced with a four-move sequence: state the football reason, name the imported tool, show its display form, then hand the quantity to the next section.
interpretation: The reason-tool-display-handoff pattern keeps the model-establishment chapter from becoming a methods catalogue by anchoring each imported concept in the problem domain.
applicability: D papers importing network science tools into a domain-specific problem.
counterevidence: The pattern breaks when the paper's imported vocabulary exceeds the prose explanation (e.g., core-periphery analysis is named but its algorithm is not described).

source_basis: Results section follows a three-phase pattern: visual scatter screening, stepwise regression, then diagnostic checks (VIF). Each phase prunes variables.
interpretation: The screen-regress-diagnose pattern gives the results section a natural rhythm: each phase answers whether to keep the variable and why.
applicability: Any results section built around variable selection.
counterevidence: The screening phase has no formal test, and the pruning rationale is inconsistent (pi1 dropped for sign, pi3 for p-value, tp2 kept despite marginal p).

source_basis: Each weakness in the evaluation traces back to one of the four assumptions made at the start.
interpretation: Mirroring weaknesses against the original assumption list closes the argument and shows the paper knows where its simplifications cost it.
counterevidence: The mirror is approximate; the weakness about pass types does not correspond directly to any stated assumption.

source_basis: The symbol table defines most quantities but explicitly defers pi and tp subscripts to the sections that use them, with a printed deferral sentence.
interpretation: Deferring rare symbols keeps the notation section compact and forces the reader to encounter each symbol in its analytical context.
counterevidence: The deferral can frustrate forward-scanning readers who want a complete symbol table upfront.

source_basis: The paper never draws its model dependency chain explicitly, but the chain (network -> centroid/dispersion/core/motifs -> indicators -> regression -> performance -> advice) is inferable.
interpretation: An implicit dependency chain can be reconstructed; an explicit diagram would have made the six-model pipeline auditable at a glance.
applicability: D papers with multi-stage model pipelines.
counterevidence: The implicit chain is correct and complete; the absence of a diagram is a missed opportunity, not an error.
